_about.what: Validation scenarios for the catalog filter (ranking). Expectations were written from combustion reasoning and the challenge text before tuning, and are the team's judgement, not NASA's.
_about.run_against_app: python3 validation/run_validation.py --target app.pipeline:rank   (any function that takes a query and returns the same dict shape)

expect_keys.top1_in: rank 1 investigation_id must be one of these
expect_keys.top_k_includes_any: at least one of these must appear in the top k (k = len(results))
expect_keys.top_k_includes_all: all of these must appear in the top k
expect_keys.top_k_at_least: [n, [ids]]: at least n of the ids appear in the top k
expect_keys.top_k_excludes: none of these may appear in the top k
expect_keys.warnings_include: scenario-level warning codes that must appear
expect_keys.warnings_exclude: scenario-level warning codes that must not appear
expect_keys.result_warnings_include: {investigation_id: [codes]} warnings that must be attached to that result if it is ranked
expect_keys.scenario: interpreted values that must match (rough-input checks)
expect_keys.assumed_fields_include: fields that must be listed as assumptions (shown to the user)
expect_keys.not_understood: the exact list of query words the scorer could not read (shown to the user)
expect_keys.query_en: English of a Korean query (not used by the check)

_about.generated_by: AI-assisted (Claude), 2026-11-14. Korean queries are user input (the page accepts Korean); query_en gives their English.

scenarios.why: The roughest input, an environment only. It is read as ISS cabin air (21%, 101.3 kPa, ventilated), and solid-material flammability investigations must come first.
A Korean alias must be read as the same preset.
The single word 'moon'. The challenge's lunar-base conditions (oxygen 30% or more, 10.2 psi or less) and the partial-gravity warning must appear.
A material only. With no environment, investigations with fabric tests (SIBAL, Nomex) must come first.
One word that signals detection. The detection profile must be used, and a SAME investigation must rank first.
An empty input must not make up a ranking; it must say what to enter.
Numbers in the sentence must override the preset.
Investigations that tested the same material (SIBAL, 75% cotton) near 21% must fill the top 3.
Lunar base at 30% oxygen. All fabric tests ran at 22% or less, so the extrapolation warning must appear, together with high-oxygen evidence (BRE, a burner that emulates a solid).
The Korean input with the same meaning as P02 must give the same top 3.
A stagnant zone with ventilation off. BRE, which emulates solid burning in still air, must be in the top 3.
A solid at high oxygen, low pressure and no flow. BRE, which tested this combination, must rank first.
A gaseous fuel at high oxygen. CFI-G, which tested propane up to 40%, must rank first.
For a detection question, SAME and SAME-R must rank first and second.
Smoke from overheated wire insulation (Kapton, Teflon) matches the SAME samples directly.

A gas-signature question. BASS-II states a combustion-product measurement purpose and measured CO and CO2, so it must rank first. Next come investigations that measured gas species (SAFFIRE: CO2 and O2). Within the tie margin they come before SAME (smoke particles), because their oxygen is recorded and SAME's is assumed.

scenarios.query: toxic gas and smoke detection in a spacecraft
scenarios.why: Both signatures are named, so investigations of either must appear: BASS-II (gas) and SAME (particles).
FLEX, which tested CO2 dilution with heptane fuel, must rank first.
BASS, which used nitrogen as the extinguishing agent, must be in the top 3.
Liquid-fuel droplet tests (FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI) must fill the top 3.

'gas jet' and 'jet flame' mean a gaseous fuel. The top 3 must be gaseous-fuel investigations, not solid tests (BASS-II, BASS, SAFFIRE-II). Until config 1.5.1 this scenario also asked for a jet-flame test (SLICE, SPICE, ACME-CLD) in the top 3. The scorer has no jet-geometry dimension, so that order came from the old tie-break. Under the tie rule of 2026-11-15 (recorded share first), SPICE and SLICE, whose atmosphere is assumed, follow the burners whose atmosphere is recorded.
'gaseous fuel' alone must be read as gas and ranked by gaseous-fuel investigations.
'droplet' is a liquid-fuel droplet. Droplet tests (FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI) must fill the top 3.
'liquid fuel' must be read as liquid, and for a lunar base the partial-gravity warning must appear with it.
An inert gas used for suppression is not a fuel. The word 'gas' alone must not make the fuel gaseous.

Detecting combustion gases is a detection question about the gas signature. The fuel must not be read as gas. Since config 1.5.0 the investigation that states a combustion-product measurement purpose and measured gas species (BASS-II, NASA BASS-II Summary Report 1.2) must rank first; until 1.4.0 this scenario expected SAME, which measured smoke particles only.
'solid' names the fuel phase (review of 2026-11-15, A3). It must be read, not left in not_understood, and the solid tests must enter the top 3.
Korean 'solid fuel' (고체 연료) names the fuel phase as well; 화재 (fire) is a generic word.
In a detection question 'CO2' names a gas signature, not a diluent or a 30% oxygen value.
'CO2 30%' is a carbon dioxide concentration. It must not be read as 30% oxygen; oxygen must be the ISS preset's 21%.

scenarios.query: smoke detector for a lunar rover
scenarios.why: A detection equipment query. It must be read as lunar-base conditions and a detection question, with a SAME investigation first and no word left unread.

scenarios.query: fire extinguisher for a Mars habitat
scenarios.why: A suppression equipment query. It must be read as a suppression question, with BASS or FLEX, which tested extinguishing agents, near the top.

scenarios.query: crew garment for a Moon base
scenarios.why: A clothing equipment query. 'garment' must be read as fabric, with fabric tests (BASS-II, SAFFIRE) near the top.
PSI has no battery tests. The ranking is the general ISS evidence, and it must say that 'battery enclosure' was not understood.

scenarios.query: water mist suppression system for a lunar habitat
scenarios.why: PSI has no water-mist suppression tests. It must be read as a suppression question but say that 'water mist' was not understood.
There is no condition to read. It must not make up a ranking, must ask for input, and must say that 'glove box' was not understood.

scenarios.query_en: lunar base at 30% oxygen and air pressure 70 kPa
scenarios.why: A Korean particle right after the unit must not hide the typed pressure: 70 kPa is the user's value, not the preset's 70.3.
A spacecraft cabin with no other environment named reads as the ISS cabin preset, so the page is not empty.

scenarios.query: a base on a planet whose atmosphere has 30% oxygen
scenarios.why: A planet that is not named is not microgravity: the partial-gravity warning must appear, and no pressure is guessed.

A spacesuit's 100% oxygen is above the highest surrounding-atmosphere oxygen tested in PSI (40%). The extrapolation warning must appear, and the investigations tested at the highest oxygen (ACME-BRE, ACME-CFI-G) must show. The oxidizer stream of inverse flames (up to 85%) is not an atmosphere and is not compared.
The challenge text gives no Martian atmosphere values. The partial-gravity warning and the request for atmosphere input must appear.
Rocket and propellant fires must be answered as out of scope.
An out-of-scope question in Korean must be treated the same way.

stability.why: Each weight is moved by plus and minus 0.05 to see whether rank 1 holds. A scenario whose rank 1 changes is reported as a close call, not as a failure.
